profile.summary: 3DMolMS (called MolMS in the FlexMS benchmark) predicts the tandem mass spectrum (MS/MS) of a compound from its 3D conformation. It takes a molecule with its precursor type and collision energy, generates a 3D conformation, encodes the atoms as a point set, and outputs a binned spectrum. The learned molecular representation can also be fine-tuned for retention time and collision cross section prediction.
profile.summary_source_locator: README.md: introduction; Bioinformatics paper abstract and Sections 2.1-2.3; FlexMS Section 3.2

summary_quotes.text: is a deep neural network that predicts the MS/MS spectra of compounds from their 3D conformations.
The molecular representation it learns transfers to related tasks such as retention time (RT) and collision cross section (CCS) prediction.
FlexMS adapts three distinct predictor paradigms: MassFormer, NEIMS, and MolMS

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: A 3D conformation is generated with the ETKDG algorithm in RDKit. Each atom becomes a point with its x, y, z coordinates and RDKit atom attributes, and bonds are represented by neighbouring vectors. In the paper, an encoder of six 3D molecular convolution layers (64 to 1024 dimensions) produces representations that are concatenated with metadata into a 2048-dimensional vector, and a decoder of five fully connected layers with residual blocks outputs the spectrum. By default spectra are binned at 0.2 resolution over m/z 0 to 1500, giving 7500 bins. Release v1.4.0 changed the encoder to aggregate over the covalent bond graph and replaced the decoder with a bidirectional head, so the current checkpoints are not the paper's architecture.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The package molnetpack has had many releases since v1.0.0 (2023-06-30). Notable changes: training data enlarged with MoNA and Waters QTOF data (v1.1.0), an Orbitrap MS/MS model (v1.1.6), an E(3)-invariant encoder (v1.3.1) and the bond-graph encoder with a bidirectional head (v1.4.0, 2026-08-11), for which all four checkpoints (QTOF, Orbitrap, RT, CCS) were retrained from geometric pretraining on ChEMBL. Release v1.4.0 has five zip assets, including a pretraining checkpoint. v1.4.0 checkpoints embed their training config and loading refuses mismatches; older checkpoints only give a warning. A result should name the package version and the checkpoint (qtof or orbitrap).

sections.title: Use in benchmarks
sections.body: The FlexMS benchmark paper (an existing source on this record) describes adapting the MolMS decoder design (fully connected layers with residual blocks) as one of three predictor heads that it pairs with different molecule embedders.

quotes.text: MolMS Predictor: An advanced encoder-decoder structure emphasizing deep residual learning [17]. The decoding block utilizes multiple fully connected layers integrated with Residual Blocks.

run_guide.summary: Install 3DMolMS from source with PyTorch and predict QTOF MS/MS spectra for the bundled example CSV; checkpoints download on first use.
prerequisites: PyTorch installed separately, matching the CUDA version (the README gives a cu124 example); a GPU is used if available, otherwise CPU.

steps.title: Get the code
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/JosieHong/3DMolMS.git
cd 3DMolMS
git checkout --detach 324f2d311c5f530967fb734489ca412781da5c67
steps.explanation: Clone the repository; the checkout line is added by Rewire to pin the reviewed commit. The clone gives the examples/ folder used below.

quotes.text: git clone https://github.com/JosieHong/3DMolMS.git cd 3DMolMS pip install .

steps.title: Install
steps.shell:
pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124
pip install .
steps.explanation: Install PyTorch for your CUDA version, then the package from source.

quotes.text: pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu124

steps.title: Predict spectra
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from molnetpack import MolNet, plot_msms

device = torch.device("cuda:0" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
molnet_engine = MolNet(device, seed=42)
molnet_engine.load_data("./examples/demo_input.csv")
pred_df = molnet_engine.pred_msms(
    path_to_results="./output_msms.mgf",
    instrument="qtof",
)
plot_msms(pred_df, dir_to_img="./img/")
PY
steps.explanation: The README's Python example, wrapped in a shell heredoc by Rewire. It downloads the QTOF checkpoint on first use.

outputs: output_msms.mgf with predicted spectra, and plots of the predicted spectra with their 3D conformations in ./img/.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
Checkpoints are cached per user (~/.cache/molnetpack on Linux, ~/Library/Caches/molnetpack on macOS).

notes: The record is named MolMS after the FlexMS paper, which cites it as 3DMolMS (Hong et al. 2023, Bioinformatics). FlexMS describes adapting its decoder design; it does not say it used the released checkpoints. The released date in structured is the change-log date of v1.4.0; the GitHub release object is dated 2026-08-12. Only the v1.4.0 release assets were saved and listed.
